The exact receiver rates are A/B RX **10.212384 / 14.894040 Mbit/s** and A/B TX **8.868608 / 9.130072 Mbit/s**. B also has fewer native RX sequence gaps and lower driver rejection/service counters. Both retain Kmem after TX and final quiet—A **+8,456 B**, B **+8,504 B**—so resource recovery remains unresolved, despite full IOB and Page recovery.

B is a promising directional candidate, with promotion still blocked. Its lower RX rejection counts, shorter service wall time and received final report support a focused follow-up, but the unmatched sender input and unresolved heap residual prevent adoption. I’m preserving the raw rows, hashes, counter scopes and FIN accounting in the statistics file, with B restoration left entirely to Root.
